root_cause.text: In `drm/vc4`’s `vc4_save_hang_state()` in `vc4_gem.c`, early error/empty-state exits returned before freeing the already allocated `kernel_state`, causing a memory leak in the hang-state capture path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces two direct returns (`if (!exec[0] && !exec[1])` and `if (!kernel_state->bo)`) with `goto err_free_state`, and adds an `err_free_state:` label that unlocks `vc4->job_lock` and calls `kfree(kernel_state)`, matching the CVE description that the previous early return path leaked `kernel_state`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Route the no-active-job case through the cleanup path in hang-state saving to ensure proper resource handling.
intent_record.what: The early return inside `vc4_save_hang_state(struct drm_device *dev)` was replaced with a jump to the existing `err_free_state` cleanup path when both `exec[0]` and `exec[1]` are null.
intent_record.how: Runtime behavior is unchanged for the no-job case in terms of skipping hang-state processing, but the function now exits through the shared error/cleanup path instead of returning directly, ensuring any necessary state cleanup is handled consistently.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix allocation-failure handling in hang-state saving by routing null `kernel_state->bo` cases through the common cleanup path.
intent_record.what: The explicit error-return block after the `kernel_state->bo` allocation check was replaced with a `goto err_free_state;` jump when `kernel_state->bo` is null.
intent_record.how: On allocation failure, execution now transfers to a shared cleanup path instead of returning immediately, allowing previously allocated state to be freed and any required teardown to occur before exiting.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix hang-state saving to properly clean up and unlock on failure instead of leaking the allocated kernel state.
intent_record.what: The function `vc4_save_hang_state(struct drm_device *dev)` was modified to add an explicit `return;` after the normal successful path, and a new error-handling label `err_free_state:` was added that unlocks `vc4->job_lock` with `spin_unlock_irqrestore(...)` and frees `kernel_state` with `kfree(kernel_state)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now has a cleanup path for failure cases where `kernel_state` must be discarded instead of leaking memory. The added label ensures the lock is released before freeing the allocated state, preventing resource leakage and maintaining correct lock handling on error.

grouping_result.intent: Fix hang-state saving to properly clean up and unlock on failure instead of leaking the allocated kernel state.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:

Author: Eric Anholt <eric@anholt.net>
Date:   Fri Oct 30 10:09:02 2015 -0700

    drm/vc4: Add an interface for capturing the GPU state after a hang.
    
    This can be parsed with vc4-gpu-tools tools for trying to figure out
    what was going on.
    
    v2: Use __u32-style types.
    
    Signed-off-by: Eric Anholt <eric@anholt.net>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/vc4/vc4_gem.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/vc4/vc4_gem.c
index 5fb0556e001e..39f29e759334 10
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in `vc4_save_hang_state()`: after allocating `kernel_state` with `kcalloc(1, sizeof(*state), GFP_KERNEL)`, the function returns early on later error/empty-state paths without freeing it. Specifically, `if (!exec) { spin_unlock_irqrestore(&vc4->job_lock, irqflags); return; }` leaks the already allocated `kernel_state`, and `if (!kernel_state->bo) { spin_unlock_irqrestore(&vc4->job_lock, irqflags); return; }` also returns without freeing `kernel_state`. There is no cleanup path at these early returns, so the memory leak is present and not fixed in this commit.
